events.title: COME OR DIE – A double bill on politics and sex
Seth Sjöström Quintet - Album Release
events.description:
Seth Sjöström (*2000) is a bass player and composer from northern Sweden currently based Berlin. With a foundation in Jazz, free improvisation and Swedish folk music, he's constantly looking for new ways to express himself as well as communicating with others through art. He's greatly inspired by the harsh but honest nature of northern Sweden and is driven by the will to use music as a tool to build a genuine connection to himself, other people and the world around him.
On the 12th of June 2026, Seth releases his new album ""Kom Hem"" together with his quintet.
Deeply personal yet widely resonant, his songwriting has connected with audiences and musicians worldwide, with his work recorded by artists from Emilia Mårtensson to the RTV Slovenian Big Band. In his own words, his music is rooted in a belief that songs can help people better understand themselves and their lives.
This special double bill brings together two singular voices in contemporary music, joined by acclaimed pianist Matt Robinson and saxophonist Adam Waldmann for an evening of evocative, boundary-crossing music.

events.description:
“Dubby DIY dance music with brilliant sound design"
Resident Advisor
”Deep, richly textured, Dub to Industrial to Clicks ’n Cuts leaning Electronics”
Hardwax
Winchester’s industrial soundscaping suggests mainframes on the fritz and nuclear cores in meltdown, dystopian sci-fi fantasies playing out on a galactic scale.”
Pitchfork
Adam Winchester is an electronic musician and live performer whose work applies dub mixing techniques to experimental electronic music. His live sets centre on the mixer as an instrument, using delay, echo, and spatial processing to reshape bass driven rhythms, found sounds, modular synthesis, bespoke instruments, feedback systems, and heavily manipulated samples in real time.
With roots in Bristol’s dubstep scene as Wedge, and a long-running practice operating between bass music and exploratory sound design, Winchester has developed a distinctive approach that prioritises space, repetition, and gradual transformation fused with tropes of Dub, IDM and the hardcore continuum. He has released on revered labels Osiris Music, Soil, and Mindwaves, with a forthcoming LP on Oval Harmonique set to drop on vinyl later this year.
Alongside solo work, his collaborative projects include Wrecked Lightship and Dot Product, with acclaimed releases on Midnight Shift, and Peak Oil, spanning experimental performance, club contexts, and installation work. His music also involves collaborations with Renate Knaup of Amon Düül II, the BBC Radiophonic Workshop, and Japanese Noise artist KK Nüll, alongside performances at festivals including Berlin Atonal, Krake, and Boiler Room.

Lajos Meinberg grew up in a family of musicians, which nurtured his love for jazz from an early age. Since 2020, he has been studying at the Jazz Institute Berlin under Wolfgang Köhler, Tino Dorado, and Bastian Stein, and has been actively involved in the Berlin jazz scene since then. He has had the opportunity to perform with musicians such as Rodney Green, Doug Weiss, Matt Wilson and Martin Wind. Lajos received the Ingolf Burkhardt Award in 2022 and won first prize at the International Jazzhaus Piano Competition in Freiburg in 2024, as well as second prize at the International Jazz Piano Competition Lausanne in 2025. In August 2023, Lajos was part of the Elbphilharmonie Jazz Academy, where he had the chance to learn from musicians like Anat Cohen, Donny McCaslin, and Sullivan Fortner.
Johann Greve is a double bassist and composer from Lower Saxony. Since moving to Berlin in 2019, he has worked as a sideman on a wide variety of projects and established himself in the young Berlin jazz scene. He has performed with Percy Pursglove, Julius Gawlik, Charlotte Greve and Olga Reznichenko, among others. In March 2024, he recorded material for his debut album with his quartet.
California-born drummer Genius Wesley is an emerging force on the international jazz scene, known for his electrifying energy, deep musicality, and fearless improvisation. A prodigy percussionist, he has already performed with jazz greats such as David Binney, Sean Jones, Buster Williams, Azar Lawrence, Gerald Clayton, and many more.

Christoph Rothmeier: percussive and electronic stuff, theremin, vocals.
Jörg Hochapfel: keyboards, guitar, glockenspiel, vocals.
The band Hunger, consisting of Christoph Rothmeier and Jörg Hochapfel, has been around since 1996, initially on Lake Constance, then for a long time in Hamburg, and finally in Berlin.
Previously known in the music world for their ""abstract pop studies with a Dadaist bent"" (taz) and ""nervous disco-punk racket"" (Tagesspiegel), they have in recent years moved into a somewhat quieter, but no less disorienting, musical territory between stumbling exotica and out-of-tune fake folk, using synthesizers, home organs, theremin, and homemade instruments.
They're bringing with them their brand-new album ""Trikotin,"" consisting of eight tracks improvised and subsequently refined in a secret French studio, available in the most practical and versatile format imaginable: a 36-page, lovingly risographed sheet music book!

As a keyboardist, producer and improviser, Dan Nicholls embraces sound as a tool for liberation, healing and joyful collectivity. Intricately crafting sound worlds which invite listeners to explore both other-worldly perceptions and the grounding and embodying nature of sound and movement, Dan's work deeply considers how sonic (and other) gestures might facilitate forms of resistance, unity and deeper understanding. 

Dan has worked as a keyboardist with Alabaster De Plume, Goldie, Shabaka, Dudù Kouate, Dali De Saint Paul, Matthew Herbert, Sarah Nicolls, Christian Marklay, Squarepusher and many more.
They co-curate the London event series 'Free Movements' and have created music and sound design for dance, film and installations.
